general.summary: Few stocks rode China’s artificial intelligence frenzy as spectacularly as model developer Z.AI Co. Now, its dramatic reversal is laying bare the vulnerabilities facing the country’s AI upstarts.

general.title: Pimco Says AI Bond Spreads May Tighten as Data Center Boom Slows
general.summary: Spreads on bonds financing the artificial intelligence build-out may tighten as a slowdown in data-center construction curbs issuance, easing some of the pressure that a flood of AI-linked debt has put on credit markets, according to Pacific Investment Management Co.

general.title: China and Canada Expand Tariff Relief as Xi Meets Carney
general.summary: China and Canada agreed to further tariff relief on agriculture and steel exports as President Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Mark Carney met in Shenzhen on Tuesday.

general.title: Barclays Says Forced Retail Selling Behind Taiwan Stock Rout
general.summary: Forced selling by retail investors was a main driver of Taiwanese stocks’ steep selloff on Monday, a trend that could extend and pressure the market further, according to Barclays Plc.

general.title: Japan Said to Delay Floating-Rate Bond Launch Given Weak Demand
general.summary: Japan will likely delay the launch of its new floating-rate government bonds as demand wanes for hedging against rising borrowing costs, with investors expecting only a few more interest-rate hikes to remain in the current cycle.

general.title: Chinese Tech Leaders Meet as US Prepares Chip Curbs
general.summary: Chinese business and technology leaders are gathering in Shenzhen ahead of the APEC CEO Summit. The talks unfold as the US Commerce Department adds licensing requirements for advanced chip sales to data centers in Southeast Asia and Brazil to close remote-access loopholes. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: New Zealand Dollar Hits Six-Year Low on Growth, Yield Gap Worry
general.summary: The New Zealand dollar fell to its lowest level since 2020 against the greenback, pressured by cooling domestic inflation expectations and a widening interest rate gap with the US.

general.title: Prediction: Nov. 18 Will Be a Huge Day for AI Power Stocks. Here’s Why. - The Motley Fool
China AI Stocks Drop as US Chip Curbs Hit Labs and Hyperscalers
general.summary: Chinese artificial-intelligence stocks tumbled Tuesday after the US moved to further restrict access to advanced chips, with the country’s biggest hyperscalers and AI model developers among the hardest hit.

general.title: Tripadvisor Loan Soars as $600 Million Payment Boosts Confidence
general.summary: Tripadvisor Inc.’s loan soared Monday as the company repaid $600 million of debt using proceeds of a sale, easing concerns for lenders as it faces a major leadership change and challenges from generative artificial intelligence tools.

general.title: Big Take: All Eyes on Anthropic’s IPO
general.summary: Anthropic’s IPO this week will be a bellwether for competitors like OpenAI and a signal of the AI industry’s health in the wake of the Nvidia scandal. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: UK Migration Advisers Reject Call for Investor Visa
general.summary: A government advisory panel has recommended that the UK ignore proposals to launch a visa route for wealthy investors, and scrap the Innovator Founder visa designed to attract entrepreneurs.

general.title: Former BOJ Chief Kuroda Sees Chance of Rate Rising Above Neutral
general.summary: Former Bank of Japan Governor Haruhiko Kuroda flagged the possibility that persistent inflation risks might prompt authorities to raise the benchmark interest rate above the so-called neutral rate, where policy is deemed to be neither stimulative nor restrictive.

Asia Data Center Hotbed Hit by US Chip Curbs as Trump Visits
general.summary: President Donald Trump is targeting Southeast Asia in Washington’s rush to tighten China’s access to the world’s most advanced chips, with his administration announcing new rules just before he travels to the region.

general.title: Gold Rises From 14-Month Low as Dip Buyers Offset Rate-Hike Bets
general.summary: Gold edged higher — after its lowest close since September 2025 — as dip buyers brought some relief from stubborn US inflation and a selloff in technology stocks.

general.title: RBA’s Bullock Says Inflation Risks Remain Skewed to Upside
general.summary: Australia still faces risks of stronger inflation at a time of geopolitical uncertainty and local capacity constraints, Reserve Bank chief Michele Bullock said, signaling policymakers remain alert to price pressures.

general.title: Anthropic Faces a Longer Wait Than SpaceX to Join Stock Indexes
general.summary: Anthropic’s planned initial public offering could generate billions of dollars in demand from index-tracking funds, though the artificial intelligence startup may have to wait longer than SpaceX did to join two major stock benchmarks.

general.title: Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness made AI bets again before October rout
general.summary: Leopold Aschenbrenner's hedge fund, which almost collapsed over the summer, bought AI stocks before shares began tumbling.

general.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Nov. 17
general.summary: Oil fell on signs supplies are outpacing demand, and as Vice President JD Vance signaled the US wants to avoid a prolonged war in Iran.

general.title: China’s Top AI Firms Limit Cyber Capabilities in Latest Models
general.summary: China’s top AI developers are releasing advanced models with reduced offensive cyber capabilities, stifling their ability to aid online attacks following a government proposal to ban such technology from being exported.

general.title: Unusual Public Feud Puts Thai Central Bank Autonomy In Spotlight
general.summary: Just three months ago, Thailand’s central bank governor said he had the backing of the board to take on a more activist role in supporting growth in the economy. Now the board’s chairman is saying he’s not moving fast enough.

general.title: Hammack Says Fed Interventions Should Be Temporary, Targeted
general.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said central bank interventions in financial markets should be temporary and targeted, signaling support for a colleague’s proposal to put asset purchases into a separate portfolio when they’re used to provide markets with emergency liquidity.
